chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed and Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about washing the deceased, so he said: 'Wash him with water and lotus (leaves). Then wash him upon the footsteps of that with another washing with water and camphor and fragrant powder if there was, and wash him for the third washing with clear water.' I said, 'Three washings for his body, all of it?' He said: 'Yes.' I said, 'There would happen to be a cloth upon him when he is washed?' He said: 'If there is capacity that there happens to be a shirt upon him, so wash him from beneath it.' And he said: 'I would love it for the one who washes the deceased if he wraps a rag upon his hand when he washes him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the steps and materials required for washing the deceased according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the canonical three-stage purification ritual for the deceased, emphasizing the use of natural purifiers like lotus (sidr) and camphor to honor the body before burial. It further refines the practical jurisprudence by recommending the deceased be washed while clothed in a shirt and instructing the washer to wrap their hand, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both ritual purity (taharah) and dignified handling of the dead.
